meta.description: How each elected executive brings a bill of their own to the body that passes it. by-request: the executive's bill is introduced by a member who agrees to carry it, as no executive may introduce one in their own name.

president.citation: U.S. Const. art. II, sec. 3 (the President shall recommend measures); only a Member may introduce a bill, House Rule XII, cl. 7, and Senate Rule VII.

governor.citation: Every state constitution's message clause (the governor recommends measures); NCSL, Inside the Legislative Process, bill introduction: bills are introduced by members, an administration's bills by a member at its request.

county-executive.citation: NACo, County Government Structure (2009): an elected county executive submits legislation for the board to introduce. Charters vary by county; per-county charter data replaces this (SG-GOV-local-executive-proposal).

mayor.citation: National League of Cities, Forms of Municipal Government: a mayor in a mayor-council city recommends ordinances to the council. Charters vary by city; per-city charter data replaces this (SG-GOV-local-executive-proposal).
